subject: Request for SLA addendum, telemetry requirements, and regional fallback plan
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@medilinkhealth.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, contracts@medilinkhealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Custom SLA addendum + telemetry for Enterprise MSA

Hi Vanessa / Contracts team,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. As we're moving toward an enterprise MSA, procurement asked that we formalize a few items as an SLA addendum attached to the order form:

- Availability target: 99.95% monthly uptime for the dedicated model endpoint (primary region US-WEST).
- Latency SLO: p95 inference latency <= 250ms for requests <= 1024 tokens (measured at service egress).
- Credits: credit schedule by hour of downtime and by degraded-latency windows.
- Telemetry: per-request IDs, per-token latency metrics, and per-route success/error counts with 30-day retention.
- Regional fallback: a defined fallback behavior and expected failover window for cross-region routing.

We're attaching our redlines to an example addendum (MediLink_Redlines_20270510.docx). We also need SOC2 evidence, an operations runbook for failovers, and a DocuSign path for the final order form. Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to the above or propose alternative language?

If helpful, procurement can do a quick 30-minute call to walk through specifics — availability any time Wednesday afternoon PST.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Director, Procurement
MediLink Health

Attachment: MediLink_Redlines_20270510.docx

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Custom SLA addendum + telemetry for Enterprise MSA

Looping in my initial legal read — I reviewed MediLink's redlines and flagged several items that need clearer definitions or alternate language:

- "Measured at service egress" is ambiguous. Propose: measured at Redwoods public API edge for the customer's account (30s aggregation window) — this ties to our telemetry.
- Credits calculation: limit to percentage of monthly fees for the affected order form (caps & aggregation window). Recommend a tiered credit schedule rather than open-ended refund liability.
- Failover: need explicit maximum RTO for regional fallback and a clause that acknowledges capacity constraints (e.g., may degrade to best-effort throughput for up to 6 hours before additional capacity is required).

I've prepared a redlined draft for the addendum (sla-addendum-annotated_kp.docx). Once we agree on the ops specifics, I'll run the external-facing language.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sla-addendum-annotated_kp.docx

From: david.kim@redwood.ai
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Custom SLA addendum + telemetry for Enterprise MSA

Technical notes from infra/ops side:

- Telemetry: we can emit a per-request UUID and per-token timing at the model-proxy boundary and expose it via a metrics endpoint (Prometheus format) and through daily S3 exports. Retention 30 days by default; longer retention can be added as a paid add-on. Sample rate: default 100% for p95 tracing, but if customers request full retention of token-level traces beyond 30d well need a storage commitment.
- Latency measurement: we measure at the egress from the serving cluster; for SLOs we use p95 over a 30-day rolling window. Need legal to accept the 30-day rolling measurement.
- Regional fallback: we can support a documented fallback policy — during a primary-region outage we will route traffic to us-east-1 as a fallback with a targeted stabilization window. Operational constraint: if capacity is constrained, we will enter a degraded-mode policy where request concurrency and batch sizes may be reduced; propose language that allows for a temporary throughput reduction (e.g., up to 30% of normal throughput) for no longer than 6 hours before we notify and engage capacity uplift.

I've attached an ops evidence & runbook spreadsheet (ops-evidence-and-runbook.xlsx) that maps required evidence for procurement (SOC2 link, runbook excerpts, oncall escalation steps).

-David
David Kim
Director, Production Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: ops-evidence-and-runbook.xlsx

Hi Olivia / Contracts team — thanks for your patience while we coordinated internally. Attached is a consolidated draft addendum (redwood-sla-addendum-vanessa-v1.pdf) that incorporates:

- Availability: 99.95% monthly uptime target (primary: us-west-2) with a defined credit schedule (see Section 3).
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms measured at Redwoods API edge, using a 30-day rolling window.
- Telemetry: per-request UUIDs and per-token timing emitted to the metrics endpoint; 30-day retention by default. Full-token-trace retention available as an add-on.
- Regional fallback: documented failover to us-east-1 with an operational degraded-mode policy (temporary throughput limits for up to 6 hours while we bring additional capacity online).
- Evidence: SOC2 report link, runbook excerpts, and a proposed DocuSign flow for the order form.

Action items / ask from MediLink:
1) Please review the attached draft and MediLink's redlines and confirm whether the draft addresses your procurement concerns.
2) If acceptable, countersign via DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/some-docusign-id.
3) Proposed quick sync to finalize language: Mon, 2027-05-17 10:00am PST — please confirm availability.

If you prefer different credit caps or a longer telemetry retention, we can route that through our commercial add-on process (would impact pricing).

Best regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
